title: ABLE: Representing and Mapping LLMs via Attribution-Based Large-model Embedding
abstract: arXiv:2606.07524v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The explosive growth of large language models (LLMs) has created a heterogeneous and poorly documented ecosystem, making systematic model comparison increasingly important for provenance auditing, security analysis, and model selection. Existing representation methods struggle to address this setting efficiently. Approaches analyzing internal parameters are powerful when architectures are compatible, but face scalability barriers under structural heterogeneity, while methods relying on external outputs may conflate models with similar behaviors and are difficult to align in richer output spaces across different tokenizers. To bridge this gap, we propose ABLE (Attribution-Based Large-model Embedding), a framework that leverages the interpretability space to construct model representations. translated_title: ABLE：基于归因的大模型嵌入方法表示与映射大语言模型
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）的爆炸式增长催生了一个异构且文档匮乏的生态系统，使得系统性模型比较在来源审计、安全分析和模型选择方面变得日益重要。现有的表示方法难以高效地应对这一场景：分析内部参数的方法在架构兼容时功能强大，但在结构异构的情况下面临可扩展性障碍；而依赖外部输出的方法可能会混淆行为相似的模型，并且在不同分词器之间更丰富的输出空间中难以对齐。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了ABLE（基于归因的大模型嵌入），一个利用可解释性空间来构建模型表示的框架。通过与分词器无关的词级对齐来聚合基于梯度的特征归因，ABLE能够捕获模型特有的输入敏感性……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: ABLE框架利用可解释性空间，通过与分词器无关的词级对齐聚合基于梯度的特征归因来构建大语言模型表示，从而在异构模型生态中实现高效的系统性模型比较。
en_tdlr: ABLE constructs LLM representations by aggregating gradient-based feature attributions via tokenizer-agnostic word-level alignment in the interpretability space, enabling efficient systematic model comparison in heterogeneous LLM ecosystems.
